observed_result.criterion: C1 before valid_before: rc 0. C1 after valid_before: rc 255 with an expiry reason in the server log. C2 (not yet valid) and C3 (expired): rc 255. The after-expiry rejection is the same with and without the agent still holding the certificate. Time from valid_before to first rejection <= 2 s + measured offset. Fail: any acceptance outside the window beyond the offset.
observed_result.summary: Observed on fixture ca1 (container-host clock offset 0.008-0.015 s): C1a (default ssh-add) and C1b (ssh-add -N) logged in before valid_before, agent-held and from disk (rc 0, Accepted line with ID). C2 refused with 'Certificate invalid: not yet valid', C3 with 'Certificate invalid: expired' (rc 255). Boundary: 153 back-to-back fresh logins, 80 accepted / 73 refused; last acceptance ended 0.029 s before valid_before, first refusal started 0.021 s before it (its authentication completed after it); none accepted starting after valid_before, none refused ending before it; all 73 refusals logged as expired. At valid_before+5 s both agents still listed the expired certificate and all four variants (agent-held/disk x default/-N) were refused as expired (rc 255). After valid_before+300 s the default-added certificate was gone from agent A (plain key kept, 1 'expiring key' line) while the -N certificate remained in agent B; the same certificate offered from disk was then refused as expired, identical to the agent-held case. Verdict pass. NEW authentication only: existing masters keep admitting sessions after expiry (G09-prelim-mux-after-expiry H1/H1b), so certificate validity does not bound live connections.

limitations: OpenSSH mechanism evidence only: host client /usr/bin/ssh (OpenSSH_10.3p1, LibreSSL 3.3.6, macOS) against sshd (OpenSSH_10.0p2 Debian-7+deb13u4, OpenSSL 3.5.6 7 Apr 2026) in disposable Docker fixture containers. No Heimdall code exists or ran; this is not evidence of Heimdall behavior.

Not desktop-lock, sleep, logout, reboot or secure-store evidence: the dedicated agents are plain ssh-agent processes in an unlocked session started by the harness. Lock continuity remains open (owner-run probes).
Single machine: macOS 27.0 arm64 with Docker Desktop (linux VM). No native Windows/WSL or Linux-host evidence. The openssh-server package version is observed, not pinned (apt floats at image build).
Fixture sshd sets PerSourcePenalties no, unlike the OpenSSH 10 default.
Requirement IDs are listed for traceability; this record is not by itself evidence that any product requirement is met (tests/evidence/README.md).
